Pop: High ollie power from Whiplash Core Profile (thinner between inserts, thicker outside) [1] 146. Press-ability: Easy to press due to Cam-Out Camber's early tip/tail rise [14] 147. Responsiveness: "Fun and responsive board that turns on the spot" [1] 148. Forgiveness: "forgiving, even after that 713.5° landing" [1] 149. Switch riding: True twin shape allows identical setup for regular and switch [1] 150. Edge dampening: Ureshred polyurethane sidewalls provide excellent dampening characteristics [15] 151. Base speed: Sintered base absorbs wax for higher on-snow speed [1] 152. Steepandcheap assessment: "hybrid camber profile and stiffer flex are rare in a park board" [43] 153. Primary competitor: CAPiTA Defenders of Awesome (DOA) — true twin, all-mountain freestyle, MSRP ~$463.95 (on sale), hybrid Resort V1 camber, carbon stringers, flex 5-6/10 [44][45] 154. Competitor: Burton Custom Camber — MSRP $679.95, directional twin, full camber, Channel mount system [46] 155. Competitor: Bataleon Disaster+ — best jib board per Inertia 2026 test, 3BT technology [47] 156. Competitor: Burton Process (comparable park/freestyle board) [48] 157. Competitor: Ride (similar price segment, comparable Slimewalls technology to Ureshred) [49] 158. Nitro T1 vs CAPiTA DOA: T1 has Cam-Out Camber (modified camber) vs DOA's Resort V1 (hybrid camber with rocker at tips); T1 flex is stiffer (7/10 vs 5-6/10); T1 has polyurethane sidewalls vs DOA's standard; T1 focused more on park/rails while DOA is more all-mountain freestyle [various] 159. Nitro T1 vs Burton: Nitro uses 2x4 insert system (universal binding compatibility) vs Burton's proprietary Channel system which limits binding choices [50] 160. Nitro brand perception: "K2 and Nitro are smart picks" for solid gear on tighter budget [51] 161. Nitro brand perception: "Nitro definitely is" a high-end brand [52] 162. Competitor pricing advantage: Nitro T1 at $529.95 is cheaper than Burton Custom at $679.95 but more than CAPiTA DOA at ~$463 (sale) [22][46] 163. vs Nitro Team: Team is directional twin with Trüe Camber and All Terrain flex; T1 is true twin with Cam-Out Camber and Park flex — Team is more versatile all-mountain, T1 is more park-focused [53] 164. vs Nitro Team Pro: Team Pro has Diamond Laminates (carbon) and faster Sintered Speed Formula II base for higher performance at speed [54] 165. vs Nitro Cheap Thrills: Cheap Thrills is softer with Flat Out Rocker for dedicated jib/rail, T1 has more pop and camber for jumps [49] 166. Shape designer: Tommy Delago [55] 167. Construction type: Sandwich sidewall construction [15] 168. Fiberglass configuration: Bi-directional (Bi-Lite = fibres in two directions) [2] 169. Core wood species: Poplar (primary) with Beech stringers [1] 170. Sidewall comparison: Similar to Slimewalls on Ride snowboards in concept [49]
